Title: UK's Prince William to be joined by wife Kate for visit to India
Article:
MUMBAI/LONDON: Kate, Britain's Princess of Wales, will undertake her biggest foreign trip since having treatment for cancer when she joins her husband Prince William in India for his annual Earthshot Prize awards this week.
Heir-to-the-throne William, 44, and Kate are flying out for a series of events across Mumbai during a three-day visit that includes Tuesday's awards ceremony.
For Kate, 44, the trip marks her most high-profile overseas visit since she had preventative chemotherapy for an unspecified form of ​cancer in 2024. While she is now in remission, she says the illness still impacts her life.
William, who, like his father King Charles, has made campaigning on the environment one of his biggest causes, founded the Earthshot Prize in 2020 with the aim of finding solutions to climate change. It awards five winners £1 million ($1.3 million) each to scale up their projects.
"For the prince, Earthshot is ultimately about replacing pessimism with possibility," a spokesperson for the couple's office at Kensington Palace said.
"It is about demonstrating that while the environmental challenges facing our planet are serious, the ingenuity, determination and creativity being applied to solving them are every bit as powerful."
CRICKET, FASHION AND CINEMA
At the awards ceremony, the royals will be joined by a number of celebrities including Indian cricketing great Sachin Tendulkar, actors Alia Bhatt and Rami Malek, and British pop group Take That, who will give their first-ever performance in India.
"To be performing here for the very first time, after all these years, and alongside the extraordinary people creating a better future for our planet - is really special," the group said in a statement.
Away from Earthshot, the royals will also meet Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Wednesday. A spokesperson for Kensington Palace said that the meeting reflected the importance of the countries' bilateral relationship in areas such as defence and tech as William develops his role on the world stage.
William and Kate will also attend events linked to Indian cricket, fashion and cinema.
Since her illness, Kate ‌has ⁠significantly reduced her official workload, saying she was taking each day as it comes. While her public appearances have gradually increased, she has not joined William on previous foreign trips.
Her only significant overseas visit since 2024 came in May when she travelled alone to Italy for two days as part of her work focusing on early childhood development.
"I was told in hospital that my recovery would not be linear. There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time," she said in an interview published this week in Country Life magazine, for which William was guest editor.
($1 = 0.7543 pounds)

Title: Golf-crazy Trump to appeal ruling keeping Washington park open
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump criticised a judge's ruling that a park in the heart of Washington must remain open to the public, after his administration sought to close it for a golf course renovation.
An avid golfer who owns courses around the world, Trump aims to turn Washington's East Potomac Golf Links, a public course with affordable rates, into a facility capable of hosting major championship-calibre events.
"Why would a judge want to delay taking a terrible and very unsafe golf course, one that is mocked all over DC (and far beyond!), instead of quickly turning it into a great and admired one?" Trump wrote on Truth Social.
The US president added that his administration will appeal the "highly destructive and political decision of the judge."
The Trump administration has called for the Nov 15 closure of East Potomac Park, a 395-acre (160-hectare) expanse where the golf course is located, to begin construction.
But a lawsuit filed by an environmental group blocked the closure, with US District Judge Ana Reyes on Saturday granting a temporary restraining order that required the park remain open for now as the lawsuit works its way through the courts.
"The Government proposes to close a historic park, daily enjoyed by Washingtonians of all stripes, indefinitely," Reyes wrote in the 30-page ruling. "This closure would irreparably harm Plaintiffs, who use the Park regularly for recreational activities."
She had previously ruled against the early demolition work conducted for the project, including the cutting down of more than 500 trees along the course.
The golf course is one of several projects launched by Trump in a bid to put his personal stamp on the US capital, such as the White House ballroom and a massive triumphal arch, despite fierce local opposition and multiple legal challenges.

Title: Those in high office must remain open to questioning, says Anwar
Article:
MANILA: Those holding high office must remain open to questioning, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said, as he highlighted the importance of parliamentary independence and reforms to the legislature's administration.
He said the Parliamentary Services Act represented a substantial reform, as it involved the executive relinquishing administrative powers over Parliament to the House and its Speaker.
"The Parliamentary Services Act precisely means that the power that's there with the Prime Minister and the government is given to the House," he said at a dinner held in conjunction with his working visit to the Philippines for the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits tonight.
Anwar said the significance of the reform was not always fully appreciated, noting that many leaders were reluctant to surrender such powers.
He added that the reforms had been debated for 30 to 40 years.
Also present were Anwar's wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul and Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony.

Title: US air travel disruptions to persist until late on Sunday
Article:
WASHINGTON: US air travel is not expected to return to normal schedules until late on Sunday, the head of the FAA said, as the aviation system gradually recovers from a nationwide flight shutdown that officials blamed on routine maintenance gone awry.
As of 9.35pm ET (0235 GMT), airlines on Saturday had cancelled more than 6,400 US flights and delayed more than 8,000, according to FlightAware, an aviation website. That followed about 9,200 flights cancelled and 7,500 delayed on Friday after the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop because of disruptions to air traffic communications. FlightAware said 875 flights scheduled for Sunday were already cancelled.
Federal Aviation Administration head Bryan Bedford said on Saturday that he expected airline operations to largely return to normal by late Sunday. He also apologised for the disruption, adding that the system remains stable.
The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop on Friday that halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours. It was the longest nationwide halt to air travel since the attacks of Sept 11, 2001, and one of the single worst US travel days ever.
The issue prompted the White House to convene an emergency meeting in the Situation Room on Friday and federal agencies to scramble to determine if it was a cyberattack. But the problem was traced to FAA contractor L3Harris' installation of at least one new router at a remote facility, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said on Saturday.
"We're working to determine whether we had incompetence, meaning was it user error or installer error from L3Harris, or did they install a faulty router? We haven't determined what the fault was," Duffy said at a press conference.
The Professional Aviation Safety Specialists, a union representing FAA safety employees, said the issue was isolated to two routers that were updated Friday. An official told Reuters it was believed the routers were in Arkansas and Texas.
An FAA official said the agency conducted a safety assessment before the work. The union said PASS-represented technicians were not involved in the upgrades that led to the ground stop.
L3Harris said it took the issue seriously and is supporting the FAA in its investigation. Its shares last traded down about four per cent after hours on Friday.
OVERLOADED COMMUNICATIONS CENTRES
Duffy said the trouble began on Friday afternoon, when air traffic control centres experienced instability in radar and communications systems. The router issue led to data overloading other communications centres, officials said.
"We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, and what that did was (it) gave us issues with our communication with aeroplanes, and it also caused some disruption with our radar," Duffy added.
The issue affected communications at 17 of the FAA's 22 en route centres, which control aircraft during the cruise portion of a flight. Bedford said the FAA ordered the ground stop in case a centre lost all communications. "No facilities went dark. Nothing was fully lost," Bedford added.
The FAA said it was doing additional testing with L3Harris to see if there are any additional risks.
Delta Air Lines, United Airlines and American Airlines all cancelled about 25 per cent of their flights on Saturday, while JetBlue cancelled nearly 45 per cent. Airlines have issued travel waivers allowing passengers to rebook flights for later dates without cost.
Though the FAA lifted the ground stop on Friday evening, the disruption for passengers was far from over, with tens of thousands of people stranded in airports. Airlines were trying to get flight crews and other personnel in position to resume flights.
The disruption stranded some college football teams on Friday before games scheduled for Saturday.
FUNDS SOUGHT TO FIX SYSTEM STRAIN
Friday's disruption is the latest and most dramatic sign of strain on a US air traffic control system beset by aging technology, equipment and communications problems and a shortage of several thousand controllers.
Duffy called on Friday for US$50 billion in funding to upgrade air traffic control systems, up from his earlier request of US$30 billion — after Congress approved US$12.5 billion last year.
House Speaker Mike Johnson told Fox News on Saturday that he supports approving more funding for air traffic this year. Johnson's Republicans control Congress until next year, when Democrats will take over because of their gains in the Nov 3 midterm elections.
US Representatives Rick Larsen and Andre Carson, Democrats slated next year to chair the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee and aviation subcommittee, respectively, said in a joint statement Saturday that their panels will "hold the administration accountable for what happened to make sure this chaos does not happen again."

Title: 'Inside Gaza': Reporting a war when it hits home
Article:
How do journalists report on a war when they become victims of the violence and when their proximity to the conflict is used to paint them as unreliable witnesses?
That's the issue explored in Inside Gaza, a new documentary that follows journalists from global news agency AFP who were trapped in the territory as Israel exacted a fearsome revenge for Hamas' Oct 7 attack.
Director Helene Lam Trong brings these news industry veterans in front of the camera, showing how they balance the difficult task of reporting on the massive military response with their own survival, as it destroys their city, killing family, friends and colleagues.
"Most international correspondents... cover a war or a news event and then return home to safety," said freelance journalist and documentary filmmaker Lam Trong in Los Angeles, where the film was shown as part of The American French Film Festival.
"Palestinian journalists could not do that. They were trapped alongside the civilian population of Gaza, with no way out; as the days passed, they themselves became victims of the war."
The Hamas-led attack on Israel on Oct 7, 2023, killed more than 1,200 people, the vast majority of them civilians. Armed men also took more than 200 people hostage.
Israel almost immediately sealed the borders of the Gaza Strip and barred international journalists from entering.
It then launched an enormous military response, pulverising swathes of Gaza in attacks that have left 73,000 people dead, according to the Hamas-run Gaza Health Ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.
Unable to send a team of reinforcements, AFP was solely dependent on the work of its local staff — experienced reporters, photographers and videojournalists, many of whom have worked internationally — to document Gaza's subsequent descent into violence and despair.
Without journalists like these, whose work was transmitted to AFP's thousands of media clients, the outside world would have had no idea what was happening inside Gaza, said Lam Trong.
In the film, which was compiled from material produced by the team on the ground, as well as from interviews conducted after they finally left, the journalists speak of the frustration of seeing their work either called into question or simply never broadcast or published.
In one sequence, the team describes their frustration at the way in which Israeli propagandists claimed genuine photos of a dead child were staged using a doll.
"At AFP, our photos, news reports and videos are used by world media outlets. But in this war, some of our images were never used," says Gaza bureau chief Adel Zaanoun.
"It worried us, even terrified us, because from the very first days, the thousand of Palestinians killed didn't count for the media."
At a time of declining engagement for traditional journalism as audiences migrate to unmoderated social media platforms and politicians seek to demonise any outlet publishing stories they do not like, Lam Trong says it is vital the public understands how newsgathering works — including the costs and the risks to those who do it.
That includes becoming targets themselves. According to the Committee to Protect Journalists and Reporters Without Borders, approximately 200 journalists have died in Gaza since the war began.
AFP's office in Gaza, which was broadcasting a live feed to clients, was hit, likely by Israeli tank fire, according to an investigation by the agency and other international media outlets.
"In Gaza, in particular, journalism and journalists have become central issues, as they have been killed, attacked and persecuted," said Lam Trong. "We do not deserve to be accused of propaganda when we conduct on-the-ground reporting."
Lam Trong, a recipient of the Albert Londres Prize — often described as the French equivalent of the Pulitzer — hopes the film, which has won numerous international awards and is eligible for Oscar contention, will spread the message of the importance of journalism.
The awards season campaign is "an opportunity to bring a very important message to Hollywood... that freedom of the press is under threat and that we must defend journalists — not just journalism, but the journalists themselves".
AFP's staff left Gaza in 2024. The agency continues its impartial coverage of the region using trusted freelance contributors.
The writer is from AFP

Title: World on cusp of lethal autonomous weapons revolution
Article:
Lethal autonomous weapons powered by artificial intelligence (AI) are set to revolutionise warfare, but there is no proper regulatory or legal framework governing the new technology.
A conference starting today at the United Nations in Geneva will discuss how to establish curbs and prohibitions on such weapons, called killer robots by some.
But some analysts doubt the discussions at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons will keep pace with the fast-changing weapons.
Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems (LAWS) "can identify, select and engage a target without the intervention of a human operator in the execution of these tasks", said Geneva Centre for Security Policy head of global and emerging risks Jean-Marc Rickli.
Autonomous weapons have long existed.
An anti-personnel mine "is an autonomous weapon in the sense that it explodes when someone steps on it", said Laure de Roucy-Rochegonde of the Centre for Geopolitics of Technology at the French Institute of International Relations.
But with the proliferation of AI-enhanced drones, such weapons are now "capable of selecting and engaging a target that was not predetermined, adapting to their environment without human intervention", said Rickli.
So the critical issue for potential regulators lies in determining the level of human control over the decision to employ such a weapon.
The United States refers to an "appropriate levels of human judgment" in the use of autonomous weapons.
France maintains that a human must remain in the decision-making loop and bans LAWS, but permits "partially autonomous" systems known as PLAWS.
"The human role is always ensured through what is termed 'appropriate control' by a military commander — a concept that varies in scope depending on the system's criticality and the operational context," said Rear Admiral Vincent Sebastien, deputy director of the French Defence Ministry's Agency for Defence Artificial Intelligence.
"We are now dangerously close to crossing a moral red line: the autonomous targeting of humans by machines," UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres and International Committee of the Red Cross president Mirjana Spoljaric warned in a joint statement in August.
But analysts said the Geneva discussions, while important, will touch only part of the issue.
Today, the diminishing role of humans is being driven by the growing use of AI in analysis and targeting.
Rickli said the scope of the agenda in Geneva is "very narrow".
"It fails to encompass the full range of issues surrounding AI on the battlefield" — an area where its use is expanding, particularly in target generation.
He said this was seen in the US-Israeli war against Iran this year "where the Americans engaged as many as 1,000 targets per day" inside Iran.
"There are a host of problems and unacceptable risks associated with targeting and decision-support systems," added de Roucy-Rochegonde.
"What kind of human supervision is required to ensure that the operator is genuinely exercising their own judgment rather than simply providing a rubber stamp for the machine's recommendations?" she asked.
The autonomous weapons to be discussed in Geneva are not yet in widespread use, although analysts have noted that they have been deployed by Russia in its invasion of Ukraine as well as US attacks in Iran.
But the spread is inevitable.
"Autonomy will very quickly become a reality on the battlefield," warned Sebastien.
"Autonomous weapon systems are not part of a distant future—a race towards greater autonomy in weapons systems is already well underway," said Guterres and Spoljaric in their statement.
Yet significant doubts and dangers remain, Dario Amodei, head of the AI giant Anthropic, warned this year: "Today, frontier AI systems are simply not reliable enough to power fully autonomous weapons."
But ultimately, the incentive for major powers is too strong.
Swarms of autonomous drones would be highly effective and some states view them as a crucial strategic advantage, said Rickli.
In January, the Chinese Defence Ministry described swarms of autonomous drones as the "new face of warfare".
"In an era of sharp military competition, the first state to normalise fully autonomous lethal strikes will reset expectations for everyone else," said Gerald Mako, a research affiliate of Cambridge University in the Small Wars Journal.
The writers are from AFP

Title: Heritage building gutted in fire in Melaka
Article:
MELAKA: A heritage building along Jalan Laksamana was gutted in a fire this evening, alarming visitors in the popular tourist area.
The fire broke out about 6pm, prompting firefighters to rush to the scene after receiving an emergency call.
Buletin TV3 reported that the affected premises were about 150 metres from an iconic historic square within the Unesco World Heritage Site.
No official details have been released on casualties, the extent of the damage or the cause of the fire.

Title: NST Leader: Coalition-building is now a political necessity
Article:
As most analysts predicted, Barisan Nasional's electoral understanding with Perikatan Nasional helped it secure an even stronger mandate in the just-concluded Melaka election.
This election offers another illustration of how the political landscape has undergone considerable changes in recent years, with traditional rivalries increasingly giving way to political cooperation and coalition-building.
BN and PN setting aside their differences to contest under a common electoral arrangement would have been difficult to imagine when both coalitions were competing fiercely for political dominance.
The nation's increasingly fragmented political landscape in recent years has made such cooperation more important, even vital, for long-term national political stability.
This is as it should be. Long-term political well-being for the country demands that responsible political groupings think outside the box with the end of rigid political boundaries.
Traditional rivalries may be making way for increasing political pragmatism all round, as parties show willingness to work with opponents as and when circumstances demand it.
Our political landscape has always demanded that political parties and their leaders appreciate coalition-building as a necessity. Negotiations and compromises are critical to make coalitions workable and durable.
This goes to show that politics as the art of the possible — which worked so well for half a century since Merdeka — is not lost on our current generation of leaders.
That said, the electorate deserves the utmost respect and regard. It expects and should get consistency and clarity. Parties must explain how their alliances reconcile with their previously-held positions and principles.
Voters should not be left guessing as to what they are actually endorsing. Flushed with overwhelming victories, coalitions may understandably want to savour their electoral honeymoons.
But they must never forget that the real test comes after elections.
Coalition-building and political compromises may work fine at the theoretical level; now comes the harder part, putting all that into practice and showing voters that a new partnership works for and in their interests.
If there is something that never goes out of fashion in Malaysia, it is political moderation in governance.
The nation has gone through thick and thin by practising the art of compromise which requires moderation, not just in views and utterances but through actions and policy implementation.
Each political alliance will need to demonstrate that it can function as an effective governing arrangement rather than simply an electoral compact that delivers the votes and wins legislative seats.
The business of government is not always headline-grabbing. In fact, it may be more about ensuring the necessary rules and laws are in place and seeing to it that they work well in everyday practice.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 74-year-old doctor missing while windsurfing off Penang
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: A search and rescue operation is underway for a 74-year-old doctor who went missing while windsurfing off Tanjung Bunga tonight.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director John Sagun Francis said the state operations centre received a distress call from a member of the public at 7.42pm.
He said five firefighters from the Bagan Jermal fire station were deployed to the scene.
"Upon arrival, the team immediately launched a surface search operation in the waters off Tanjung Bunga," he said in a statement tonight.
John said a forward control post had been set up to coordinate the search.
The operation is ongoing, with assistance from the police and Civil Defence Force personnel.

Title: US ties will not stop Malaysia from engaging China, says Anwar
Article:
MANILA: Malaysia's relationship with the United States will not prevent it from engaging independently with other countries, including China, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
He said foreign investments must operate within Malaysia's national policy framework and respect the country's interests as it navigates an increasingly uncertain geopolitical environment.
"You are an investor; you can decide what to do, but it must be through our framework, our national policy, and the protection of our interests as a nation," he said at a dinner held in conjunction with his working visit for the 49th Asean Summit here tonight.
Also present were Anwar's wife, Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul and Malaysian Ambassador to the Philippines Datuk Abdul Malik Melvin Castelino Anthony.
Anwar said he had conveyed Malaysia's independent position during a telephone conversation with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio about a week and a half ago, during which issues involving data centres, chips and artificial intelligence were discussed.
He said the assurances given during the conversation did not prevent Malaysia from making its own decisions on engagement with other countries, including China.
Anwar said the Asean Summit also provided an important opportunity to chart the region's course through a turbulent period marked by geopolitical uncertainty.
He said engagement with different global powers reflected Malaysia's foreign policy approach and Asean centrality, adding that smaller countries needed to navigate the challenging circumstances carefully.
On the economy, Anwar said attracting investments and securing projects must go hand in hand with good governance and efforts to prevent abuse of power.
"Good governance is central to me," he said, reaffirming his commitment to policies aimed at combating corruption.
He said Malaysia should be recognised not only for its vibrant economy but also for its firm stance against abuse of power and endemic corruption, which ultimately caused hardship for ordinary people.

Title: Man arrested after brandishing knife at security guards in Wisma Darul Aman
Article:
ALOR SETAR: A man was arrested after allegedly brandishing a knife at security guards at Wisma Darul Aman here after entering the premises without stopping at the security checkpoint this morning.
The 45-year-old suspect, who was riding a grey Yamaha Ego Gear scooter, is believed to have entered the building's compound alone at 8.10am.
Kota Setar police chief Assistant Commissioner Syed Basri Syed Ali said a 29-year-old security guard who noticed the incident gave chase and stopped the suspect to ask about his presence at the premises.
However, the suspect suddenly pulled a small black knife from his right trouser pocket and pointed it at the guard and his colleague.
"The suspect tried to flee but was apprehended by the complainant with the help of the other security guard before police were called.
"Police who arrived at the scene arrested the suspect and seized a knife measuring about 15cm, together with its sheath.
"Checks found that the suspect had no previous criminal record, but a urine screening test returned positive results for methamphetamine and amphetamine," he said in a statement today.
Syed Basri said the suspect, who was taken to Alor Setar police station for further action, was from Kampung Berjaya here.
A body search found no other prohibited items or drugs on him.
He said police had recorded a statement from the complainant, who reported a brief struggle during the attempt to apprehend the suspect and seize the knife.
The case is being investigated under Section 6(1) of the Corrosive and Explosive Substances and Offensive Weapons Act 1958.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: DOE investigates two-day spike in unhealthy air quality at Batu Muda
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Department of Environment (DOE) is investigating a rise in the Air Pollutant Index (API) at its Batu Muda Air Quality Monitoring Station here, which has recorded unhealthy readings of above 150 for the past two days.
In a statement today, DOE said investigations began on Nov 14 and involved inspections of the monitoring station, field patrols and efforts to identify possible sources of air pollution in the surrounding areas.
Preliminary inspections found that the station was operating normally.
"However, further checks are being carried out to verify the recorded readings.
"Field patrols identified two small-scale open burning incidents, which were extinguished on the same day.
"Despite this, the API reading at Batu Muda remained above 150, while the nearby Cheras station recorded a reading of about 60," it said.
DOE said further investigations were underway to identify factors contributing to the difference in readings between the two stations.
"As part of the verification process, DOE has instructed the installation of additional air quality monitoring equipment near the Batu Muda station to obtain supporting data for technical analysis.
"Preliminary findings will be shared after 24 hours of monitoring and technical checks.
"Drone surveillance is also being conducted to help identify possible sources of air pollutant emissions, including open burning activities in the surrounding areas," the statement said.
DOE reminded the public not to engage in open burning or allow their land or premises to be accessed by irresponsible individuals who might start fires, whether deliberately or accidentally.
It said those convicted of open burning under Section 29(A) of the Environmental Quality Act 1974 could face a fine of up to RM1 million, imprisonment of up to five years, or both.
Compounds of up to 50 per cent of the maximum fine could also be imposed for each offence.
The public can report open burning or fires to the Fire and Rescue Department or DOE at its toll-free hotline, 1-800-88-2727.

Title: Kepong nightclub destroyed in fire
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: An entertainment outlet in Jalan Metro Perdana Barat, Kepong, was almost completely destroyed in a fire today.
Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ahmad Mukhlis Mokhtar said firefighters from five stations and three voluntary fire brigades were deployed after receiving an emergency call at 11.23am.
"About 90 per cent of the 594-square-metre nightclub was destroyed.
"The cause of the fire is still under investigation, and no casualties have been reported so far," he told a press conference at the scene today.
He said the premises owner informed the department that everyone inside had been instructed to evacuate before the fire spread.
Earlier, videos of thick black smoke billowing from the nightclub in Kepong circulated on social media.

Title: Sanusi hopes BN-PN cooperation continues into GE16
Article:
ALOR SETAR: The cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) should continue into the 16th General Election (GE16), following their combined success in the Melaka state election yesterday.
PN and PAS central election director Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said he hoped the cooperation would continue, as it appeared to have received support from the majority of voters.
"We won many more seats than before. I hope so (that the cooperation continues in the next general election)," he said when met after tabling the Kedah 2027 Budget at Wisma Darul Aman here today.
In the 16th Melaka election, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured four and PN won three.
The results gave BN and PN a combined 24 seats, securing more than a two-thirds majority in the Melaka state assembly.
Sanusi, who is also Kedah Menteri Besar, said the outcome also carried a message for the parties concerned, as voters had made their assessment of the current political landscape.
Asked about his relatively limited campaigning in Melaka this time, he said he had to focus on preparations for the Kedah 2027 Budget, which required detailed scrutiny.
"I had to focus on the Kedah 2027 Budget because it was longer and more detailed.
"We needed to concentrate fully on the budget presentation, so I did not have time to go to Melaka. But there were many others who helped with the campaigning," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three Malaysians fined 12,000 baht over traffic obstruction in Hat Yai
Article:
SONGKHLA: Three Malaysian tourists were fined a total of 12,000 baht (about RM1,447) by Thai police after they were caught obstructing traffic and making illegal vehicle modifications along Phetkasem Road in Hat Yai early today.
Hat Yai Police Station deputy traffic inspector Police Lieutenant Prut Pattanapran said the three men, aged between 26 and 30, were summoned to the police station along with a Thai national following public complaints about their conduct.
He said the incident occurred at 12.30am and involved three Malaysian-registered cars, in blue, red and white, and a black car belonging to the Thai national, travelling in a convoy along the road.
"The driver of the black car at the front was believed to be recording a video for social media content, while the group of vehicles made several U-turns, revved their engines loudly and obstructed traffic," he told reporters today.
Prut said their actions angered local residents before footage of the incident went viral on social media.
"The group of tourists was believed to have been recording social media content while carrying out these stunts and may not have been aware of Thailand's traffic regulations," he said.
He said all four individuals pleaded guilty and paid fines of 4,000 baht (about RM482) each before being released today.
Prut advised foreign tourists to understand, respect and comply with Thai laws throughout their stay to avoid breaking the law.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kedah civil servants to receive RM3,000 special aid
Article:
ALOR SETAR: Kedah civil servants and members of the state administration will receive RM3,000 in special financial assistance in appreciation of their service and dedication.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor said the assistance would benefit 5,031 recipients and be paid in three instalments in December this year, February and August next year.
"The close cooperation between the political leadership and the administrative machinery is key to our success in developing the state of Kedah, which we love.
"In appreciation of their hard work, I am pleased to announce that the state government has approved this special financial assistance, involving a total allocation of RM15 million," he said when tabling the Kedah 2027 Budget at the Kedah State Legislative Assembly here.

Title: Voter support alone not enough to form government, says Amirudin
Article:
KLANG: Increased voter support alone is insufficient to form a government, with cooperation between political coalitions proving to be a decisive factor, says Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari.
The Pakatan Harapan (PH) election director said forming a government required more than just election strategies, as political parties also needed to reach an understanding and work together with other coalitions.
He said preliminary results of the Melaka state election showed positive gains in support, particularly among Malay voters and younger people.
However, he said the gains were not enough to secure a stronger position for PH.
"There were some fairly positive increases for certain parties, particularly in Malay votes, which we can discuss.
"But it is not enough because the issue is not just about coalitions or support for a coalition, but how political alignments should be considered to form a government.
"In the end, the formula for success in Malaysia is through a successful coalition. Today, coalitions are no longer just between political parties, but between coalitions themselves. This is something our leaders must consider carefully," he said.
He was responding to questions on changes in support for PH following the Melaka election.
Amirudin, who is also Selangor menteri besar, was speaking after officiating the 2026 National PIBKS Digital Education Carnival here today.
Asked whether PH needed to change its political strategy, he said support for the coalition remained intact and had increased in several areas.
However, he said he had yet to obtain the detailed Melaka election results to conduct a comprehensive assessment of PH's performance.
In the 16th Melaka state election yesterday, BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) won a combined 24 of the 28 state seats, securing more than a two-thirds majority in the state assembly.
According to official Election Commission results, BN won 21 seats, PN secured three, while PH won four.

Title: Heavy rain floods homes in 2 Penang villages [WATCH]
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Heavy rain flooded homes and access roads in two Penang villages today, as water levels rose rapidly in low-lying areas.
The affected areas were Kampung Tasik Junjung in Simpang Ampat and Kampung Sulup in Teluk Kumbar.
No evacuations had been reported.
TikTok live broadcasts showed residents in Simpang Ampat moving their belongings to higher ground.
Floodwaters also entered several homes in Kampung Sulup, Teluk Kumbar.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department had earlier issued a thunderstorm and heavy rain warning for several states, including Penang, during the ongoing northeast monsoon transition. Rain continued in several parts of the state.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No pressure on Anwar to dissolve Parliament, says Dzulkefly
Article:
SEREMBAN: There is currently no pressure on Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to dissolve Parliament to pave the way for the 16th general election (GE16), says Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said the prime minister had his own considerations on the appropriate time to dissolve Parliament, adding that the Federal Government's current term had yet to expire and Anwar continued to enjoy majority support among members of parliament.
"I think we should wait. There is no pressure to make any sudden move to dissolve Parliament.
"We should wait until the end of the term, unless something drastic happens. We should prioritise the positive economic momentum that the people are enjoying today," he told reporters after officiating the 2026 National Wanita Muda Amanah Convention (Warda) at Klana Resort here today.
Dzulkefly, who is also health minister, was commenting on calls for Parliament to be dissolved following the Melaka election, in which BN and PN secured a combined 24 seats while Pakatan Harapan (PH) won four.
He said the people should first be given the opportunity to enjoy the benefits of the Unity Government's efforts, citing positive economic indicators, foreign investments and rising household incomes.
He also said Malaysia's economic performance had received recognition from international analytical bodies, claiming the country ranked among the world's 15 best-performing economies after climbing 19 places.
Dzulkefly said any move that could undermine political and economic stability or national harmony was undesirable, adding that the people's well-being should remain the priority.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jordan sentences three men to death over deadly church attack
Article:
AMMAN:  Jordan's State Security Court sentenced three men to death on Sunday for carrying out an attack on a church in the southern governorate of Karak last month that killed nine people, the state news agency Petra reported.
The court convicted the men of offences including carrying out terrorist acts resulting in death, possessing weapons and ammunition for terrorist purposes and promoting the ideology of a terrorist group. The ruling is subject to appeal and automatic review by the Court of Cassation, Petra said.
Gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud on October 23, in a rare attack on Jordan's Christian minority. Authorities said 34 people were also wounded.
Security forces arrested the three men on October 26 after a shootout at an abandoned house in Karak. All three were wounded, while no security personnel were injured, according to the Public Security Directorate.
Jordan, a US partner in the fight against extremism, later that day launched airstrikeson southern Syria against groups it linked to the church attack. Syrian authorities said seven people, including three children and a woman, were killed.
Jordan later acknowledged that its airstrikes had killed civilians in Syria and the two countries agreed to form a joint security committee to review the incident and its consequences. — REUTERS
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Health Ministry targets full capacity at Pasir Gudang Hospital
Article:
SEREMBAN: The Health Ministry will prioritise efforts to bring Pasir Gudang Hospital in Johor to full operational capacity, from its current level of 85 per cent.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was implementing an aggressive plan to fill vacant positions to ensure the hospital could operate at full capacity, with 304 beds and 16 delivery rooms.
He said the placement of nurses and medical specialists at the hospital was currently based on its operational capacity.
"Our current operational level is 85 per cent. I have already answered this matter in Parliament. We have not been able to fill all the positions for doctors and specialists.
"However, the current placement of specialists and doctors allows us to operate at 85 per cent. Many departments have already begun operating," he told reporters after officiating the Amanah National Young Women's Convention 2026.
Earlier, the media reported that Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi had raised concerns over the hospital's operational needs.
Of the 2,271 positions allocated to the hospital, only 1,276 had been filled as of Nov 6.
Dzulkefly said the ministry remained committed to meeting Johor's healthcare needs.
Located in Bandar Seri Alam, Pasir Gudang, the hospital began operations in stages on Aug 1, 2025.
Its construction cost RM375.5 million and was aimed at improving access to healthcare for residents of Pasir Gudang and surrounding areas, while helping to ease congestion at Sultanah Aminah Hospital and Sultan Ismail Hospital.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 40-year-old structure caused Kuala Kangsar water tank burst
Article:
IPOH: The bursting of a 455-cubic-metre water tank at Taman Kuala Kangsar yesterday was caused by the deterioration of its structure, which was more than 40 years old.
Perak Infrastructure, Energy, Water and Public Transport Committee chairman Datuk Seri Mohammad Nizar Jamaluddin said the Perak Water Board's (LAP) Kuala Kangsar operations centre received information about the incident about 5pm.
The incident affected water supply to about 520 consumers in the surrounding areas.
He said LAP had carried out cleaning works on roads around the damaged tank, while direct water supply through the main pipeline had been provided to the affected areas of Taman Kuala Kangsar and Taman Meranti.
"The removal of all affected tank panels has been carried out, and plans are being made to replace the tank with a new one.
"In addition, LAP is conducting a comprehensive technical assessment of the old tank structure before installation of the new tank begins," he said in a statement today.
Nizar said preliminary investigations at the scene found that water from the burst tank had overflowed onto surrounding roads, but no casualties or property damage had been reported.
"An inspection of the house nearest to the tank also found that it was safe and had sustained no damage," he said.
He said water supply to the affected areas remained stable and uninterrupted, while LAP's Kuala Kangsar operations centre would continue monitoring the situation to prevent further disruptions and ensure the incident did not recur.
Several videos of the incident have gone viral on social media since yesterday, causing panic among residents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Megaspeed says Alice Huang left company in August 2025
Article:
SINGAPORE: Megaspeed said on Sunday that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, whose ties to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang raised US national security concerns, had officially left Megaspeed on Aug 30, 2025, and had no current role at the Singapore-based company.
"Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang's personal and private matters," the company added in a statement.
"Megaspeed is aware of recent media reports containing assertions about our business, supply chain and global operations that are not supported by verifiable evidence."
The company said it conducted "legitimate and lawful business" and had retained external legal counsel to conduct a thorough internal investigation.
On Friday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that four government agencies favoured putting Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the heart of the Nvidia scandal, on a trade black list but not the Commerce Department that was in charge.
Bessent said Treasury, Pentagon, the State Department and the US Trade Representative's Office had favoured adding Megaspeed to the Commerce Department entity list for months.
"But Commerce has the pen," Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box." "You will have to ask them about their internal processes."
The Commerce Department's so-called entity list is a trade blacklist of groups connected to China that US officials say pose national security risks.
The department did not immediately return a request for comment.
There is growing criticism of Secretary of Commerce, Howard Lutnick's role in overseeing export controls on US chips to China.
Lutnick reportedly stalled President Donald Trump's crackdown on companies suspected of diverting Nvidia's ‌chips to China, media outlets reported this week.
Republican Senator John Curtis said that "Secretary Lutnick's reported stalling on export controls raises the question of whether the Commerce Department is acting in the best interests of the American people."
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN plans to field PPP candidates in next general election
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional plans to field People's Progressive Party candidates in the next general election, subject to agreement from MIC's top leadership.
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the plan would require the agreement of MIC president Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran and deputy president Datuk Seri M Saravanan.
"I am determined that, with the agreement of Tan Sri Viki (Vigneswaran) and Datuk Seri Saravanan, we will field PPP candidates in the next general election," he said at the PPP Deepavali open house here today.
In January, PPP, previously known as MyPPP, was readmitted as a component party of the coalition.
Zahid said he respected PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan for keeping the party in BN.
He also referred to BN's recent election victories in Johor, Negri Sembilan and Melaka, saying that despite differences of opinion, the coalition had come together again as one family.
"In a football tournament, three wins in a row is a hat-trick. This is a very stylish victory for BN.
"This is a people's movement. It is also divine intervention," he said.
He said BN had to work hard and smart but, most importantly, show care and courtesy to all Malaysians, regardless of religion, race, ethnicity or language.
"We do not need to shout and scream or keep saying 'sakau' here and there.
"We talk about the good things. Let people say what they want about us, but we will speak well of ourselves. This is the beauty of BN," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nearly 1,500 migrants arrive in Canary Islands in one day
Article:
MADRID: Almost 1,500 migrants arrived in Spain's Canary Islands on Saturday, the highest number in a single day since 2020, the EFE news agency reported on Sunday, citing the maritime rescue service.
A total of 1,488 people in 14 boats were rescued by the Spanish coastguard, EFE reported, continuing a surge of arrivals from West African countries to the Spanish archipelago since October.
The previous one-day record was the 1,461 people rescued in waters off the Canary Islands on Nov 7, 2020, maritime rescue services said on Sunday.
While migrant arrivals have declined so far this year compared with the same period last year, the sharp increase last month placed additional pressure on reception and emergency services on some of the Canary Islands, particularly the smaller and less densely populated ones.
One boat on Saturday was carrying 240 people, including 12 women and 36 children, authorities said. The rescued migrants were taken to El Hierro, one of the smallest Canary Islands.
Most of the people were from Senegal, Gambia and Guinea Conakry.
Twelve boats arrived in El Hierro, plus one in Gran Canaria and another in Tenerife.
Spain's Territorial Policy Minister Angel Victor Torres will visit El Hierro on Sunday to discuss the surge in migrant arrivals.
The Atlantic route from West Africa to the Canary Islands is one of the world's deadliest migration crossings.
Thousands of migrants attempt the journey each year in overcrowded boats, seeking to reach Spanish territory despite rough seas, strong currents and long distances.
Arrivals tend to pick up in the autumn months, when sea conditions along the route are generally calmer and more favourable for crossings.
Migrant arrivals to the Canary Islands between January and Oct 31 were down 5.5 per cent from the same period last year, government data show.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Indonesia was frank on steps taken over forest fires, Asean chair says
Article:
MANILA: The Philippines' foreign minister said on Sunday that Indonesia was very candid in expressing what it had done to address forest fires.
"The leaders also encouraged the Asean member states to prioritise the ratification of the Asean Coordinating Center on Transboundary Haze Pollution Control," Foreign Minister Theresa Lazaro told a news briefing.
On Friday, a study said thousands of hectares of land on palm oil and pulpwood concessions run by large listed firms were burnt during Indonesia's worst fire season in years, highlighting the role of deforestation and land clearing.
Indonesia's forest fires caused a spike in respiratory illness at home and triggered air pollution warnings and school closures across the region, with fire emissions surging to three times the seasonal average.
A total of 2.88 million hectares of land were damaged by fire from January to October this year, driven by intense El Nino weather conditions and extreme heat, as well as clearing of forests to make way for industrial-scale palm oil and pulpwood plantations, according to a joint study by Rainforest Action Network (RAN) and geomonitoring platform Nusantara Atlas.
Another report quoting scientists said, wildfires that hit large parts of Indonesia from August to October and plunged much of Southeast Asia into hazardous smoke were made much worse by "record-breaking" heat caused by human-induced climate change.
While a very strong El Nino was the dominant factor in determining the extremely low levels of rainfall across Indonesia from July, human-induced climate change contributed around 1.6 degrees Celsius of additional heat during the fire season, said a report by climate research group World Weather Attribution.
"The conditions that we saw this year would simply just not have happened in a world without the human contribution to climate change, even with the very strong El Nino that we're seeing," said Theodore Keeping, a researcher into wildfires and extreme weather at Imperial College London who contributed to the report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 1,606 flood victims remain at relief centres in 3 states
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,606 flood victims from 432 families remained at nine temporary relief centres in Selangor, Perak and Sarawak as of 4.30pm.
The Social Welfare Department's Info Bencana portal recorded the highest number of evacuees in Selangor, with 1,408 people from 373 families housed at seven centres in Kuala Selangor.
In Perak, 191 people from 58 families were staying at two centres in Hilir Perak.
In Sarawak, seven people from one family remained at a relief centre in Miri.
Of the total evacuees, 497 were adult women, 475 adult men, 270 girls, 316 boys, 32 baby boys and 16 baby girls.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Buried under hot tar, 11-year-old Hasya Fahira needs surgery
Article:
BATU PAHAT: An 11-year-old girl who lost both parents when a tar-laden lorry crushed their multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) in Parit Yaani will undergo plastic surgery for injuries to her left thigh.
Johor Islamic Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Khalid said specialists from Sultanah Aminah Hospital (HSA) would be brought to Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI) to perform the procedure, sparing the girl, Hasya Fahira Zulkifli, from having to be transferred.
He said her injuries were more severe than those sustained by her younger brother, Muhammad Adam Mohd Hardi, 8, after both children were buried under hot tar in the Nov 1 accident.
"The Johor Islamic Religious Council (MAIJ) will cover all costs involved, including any additional expenses," he said after accompanying Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi on a visit to the siblings at HSNI today.
Onn Hafiz also celebrated Hasya Fahira's birthday, which falls today.
Fared said arrangements were also being made for both children to receive survivors' pensions from the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), as their late father had previously worked and contributed to the scheme.
Pending approval, MAIJ would provide monthly living assistance to their uncle, who is caring for the siblings.
He said the state government was also prepared to cover any additional expenses arising from the children's needs.
In the 12.30pm accident, the children's parents, Tengku Syafirana Tengku Abdullah, 44, and Mohd Hardi Mohd Husin, 46,
were killed
when a tar-laden lorry overturned and crushed their MPV along Jalan Yong Peng-Muar near Parit Yaani.
The lorry had reportedly suffered a burst tyre.
Hardi sustained head and arm injuries, as well as burns to several parts of his body, while his wife suffered severe head and internal injuries, as well as burns.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Urgent climate finance pleas at COP31 face a non-urgent response
Article:
URGENT pleas for cash from poor nations most exposed to the kind of climate-related disasters that have marked this year risk meeting a sluggish response at Turkiye's COP31 talks as Western governments put national security and living costs first.
Two years ago, rich countries agreed at UN climate talks they would triple climate funding for poorer countries to US$300 billion per year by 2035 versus a previous 2020 target.
Also by 2035, financing from all public and private sources combined would be US$1.3 trillion annually.
The rich countries met their 2020 target two years late.
Since then, climate action has slipped down the political agenda for Western governments as US President Donald Trump has withdrawn international funding, while wars in Ukraine and the Middle East have added to inflationary pressures and the need to spend on security.
Vulnerable small island nations say the cash they need to repair damage and to guard against future climate-related crises is again arriving too slowly and their own budgets have shrunk.
"Like many small island developing states, we remain in a perpetual climate disaster recovery mode," Solomon Islands Prime Minister Matthew Wale told the conference. "We cannot build resilience while our fiscal space erodes."
Even when money is available, technical hurdles set by lenders can stretch the administrative capacity of small states.
For many developed nations, facing international and domestic unrest as citizens protest against the rising cost of living, their focus has narrowed.
Britain, which has sought to be a leader in addressing climate change, said in July savings made from switching some climate finance contributions from grants to loans would be used to help fund a cap on domestic bus fares.
Meanwhile, defence spending has climbed significantly.
The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute estimated in April that world military expenditure reached US$2.89 trillion in 2025, up 2.9 per cent in real terms from 2024.
Marshall Islands President Hilda Heine said military defence ultimately was the smaller concern.
"We are told there is no money, but as spending on war grows, the greatest security threat we face remains underfunded. I appeal to you: Find money for life, not death," she said in her speech to the conference in the Turkish Mediterranean city of Antalya on Wednesday.
COP31 SEEKING IMPLEMENTATION, NOT NEW TARGETS
As they respond to the contemporary mood, host country Turkey and lead negotiator Australia have emphasised making previous pledges work, rather than securing a new headline target at the conference, which continues until the end of next week.
"COP31 must respond to the global moment and send a clear message to accelerate implementation," Australia's COP31 negotiating president Chris Bowen said. He also said finance must be "faster, simpler and fairer."
[[nid:1578415]]
Analysis by previous COP host Brazil published earlier this week found that US$137 billion was mobilised in 2024, a slight increase on 2023, but that direct aid and future commitments to multilateral funds were lower.
Current trends suggested provision would fall US$840 billion short of the US$1.3 trillion goal, it said.
"Geopolitical tensions, constrained fiscal space in many developing countries and the high cost of capital where it is most needed are among the obstacles," the report said.
By way of solutions, it urged measures such as risk-sharing and clearer links between national plans and budgets.
Some smaller nations have taken novel steps to find cash and to spur richer nations to match it.
The Solomon Islands pledged US$400,000 from its own pocket on Thursday, saying it was determined to show leadership and calling on rich countries to do the same.
The Bahamas committed US$75 million to protect and restore its seagrass meadows, which store carbon, to try to persuade investors to fund verified carbon projects.
UNCLOGGING THE SYSTEM TO GET MONEY FLOWING
Both public and private funding provide climate finance grants, loans, aid and investment in measures ranging from renewable energy to flood defences.
Multilateral development banks are a conduit for finance that leverages capital provided by shareholder countries to increase lending power and they say they are delivering.
Their lending reached record levels in 2025, according to the European Investment Bank.
But, they could do more, according to Washington-based think tank the Center for Global Development and recipients of the finance have said the development banks should make access easier.
Addressing that, a group of multilateral funds told the COP31 talks they would rely more on one another's assessments in co-financed operations rather than having to go through multiple overlapping processes.
For private investors, the most obvious issue is the risk of investing in an instrument that does not guarantee returns.
Given how unforthcoming the world's richer governments have been, the private sector is ever more important.
"Our clients see opportunities in the energy transition, but they need reliable power, predictable costs and confidence in customer demand before they invest," HSBC Chief Sustainability Officer Julian Wentzel said.
"COP31 needs to help create that confidence."
* The writers are from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From 328 to 56: Selangor flood hotspots down 82.9pc in 10 years, says MB
Article:
KLANG, Nov 15 — The number of flood hotspots in Selangor has dropped significantly by 82.9 per cent, from 328 areas in the 2016/2017 period to just 56 locations this year, following the implementation of various mitigation measures as well as continuous improvement of the drainage system by the state government.
Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said all the remaining high-risk locations identified were now being given special attention through an allocation for 47 mitigation projects aimed at reducing the impact of floods.
“We will focus on the 56 identified hotspots because the efforts we have undertaken in Selangor have proven effective in reducing and addressing flooding, including in Kampung Bukit Lanchong and Taman Sri Muda in Shah Alam, as well as several other areas.
“But we are now in the early stages of the monsoon transition, so we may have to see how it develops from time to time,” he told reporters after officiating at the launch of the 2026 National Digital Education Carnival for Parent, Community and Private Sector Engagement (PIBKS) at Klang Parade Mall here today.
Also present were Ministry of Education (MOE) Daily School Management Division director Mohd Hanafi Samad and Selangor Education director Wan Nor Ashikin Abu Kassim.
Elaborating on the scope of the initiative, Amirudin said long-term plans were also being drawn up to address drainage problems in the Parit Mahang area in Kuala Selangor.
“This is an ongoing initiative and, certainly, three key areas have been identified, namely Kampung Melayu Subang, Kubu Gajah and Puncak Alam, which are being given attention as they have been affected by flooding, even during the early phase of the monsoon transition.
“Several districts which used to be badly affected, such as Dengkil, Kuala Langat and Hulu Langat, are now in a much more controlled situation following effective maintenance works and infrastructure upgrading carried out,” he added.
Earlier, the media reported that 1,399 evacuees from 370 families were still sheltering at six temporary relief centres in Kuala Selangor as of this afternoon, compared with 1,493 victims from 398 families this morning.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, the Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Mahang relief centre had the highest number of evacuees, at 420, followed by SK Dato’ Maharaja Lela (391), Sekolah Rendah Agama (SRA) Bukit Kuching (287), Bukit Kuching Tengah Community Hall (119), Kafa Integrasi Hidayah Bukit Cherakah (114) and SRA Batu 8 Ijok (68). — Bernama

Title: Woman dies in two-car collision near Kota Tinggi after vehicle veers into oncoming traffic
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 15 — A 60-year-old woman was killed in an accident involving two cars at Kilometre 45 of Jalan Johor Bahru-Mersing near Kota Tinggi today.
Kota Tinggi district police chief Supt Yusof Othman said police received information from the public about the incident at 2 pm.
He said the accident involved a Toyota Vios driven by a 33-year-old man and a Proton Saga driven by a 28-year-old woman.
Yusof said the victim, who was the female driver’s mother, was travelling in the car with the driver’s two daughters, aged seven and five.
“Initial investigations found that the accident occurred when the Toyota Vios entered the opposite lane before colliding with the Proton Saga,” he said in a statement today.
He said the accident left the victim, who was seated in the rear right passenger seat, with severe internal injuries, and she was pronounced dead at the scene.
“The drivers of both vehicles and the children were taken to Kota Tinggi Hospital for further treatment,” he added.
Meanwhile, the victim’s body was sent to the Forensic Unit of the same hospital for further procedures. The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Zahid: Negeri Sembilan royal dispute to be resolved soon, in line with state constitution
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said the dispute involving the Negeri Sembilan royal and the state administration will be resolved soon in accordance with the state constitution.
He said the primary goal is to ensure the state administration runs smoothly for the people’s sake, according to a report by
The Star.
“The problems in Negeri Sembilan will be resolved as soon as possible,” he said after attending the People’s Progressive Party (PPP) Deepavali open house.
“We will do whatever necessary, provided that the problems faced by the people of Negeri are resolved and that the state administration runs smoothly and operates in accordance with the state constitution.”
The crisis began with a dispute between the four Undang and the 11th Yang di-Pertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, over who should be the state’s ruler.
Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim confirmed on September 17 that the state executive council backed an April 17 proclamation to unseat Tuanku Muhriz, which had been signed by one Undang and three other ruling chiefs whose positions were in dispute.
Ismail then sent a formal letter to the Conference of Rulers declaring Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the “new” Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
However, the state government officially withdrew that letter yesterday, reaffirming its commitment to uphold the state constitution and customary traditions.
The retraction took into account a statement issued by the Malay Rulers on October 14 as well as a Seremban High Court order dated June 5, which maintained the status quo regarding Tuanku Muhriz’s position.
Ismail said the decision to retract the letter was made to uphold the supremacy of the Laws of the Constitution of Negeri Sembilan 1959 and preserve the order of constitutional monarchy.

Title: ‘We won big’: Sanusi wants PAS-led Perikatan-BN partnership to carry on to GE16
Article:
ALOR SETAR, Nov 15 — PAS leader Datuk Seri Muhammad Sanusi Md Nor today said Perikatan Nasional (PN) and Barisan Nasional (BN) should carry their partnership into the 16th general election after their win in the Melaka state election.
Sanusi, who is both PN and PAS election chief, said he hoped to see that happen after seeing how the majority of voters accepted the pairing,
Berita Harian
reported this evening.
“Alhamdulillah, we won big, more than before. I hope that is how it will be [for the cooperation to continue in the next general election],” he was quoted telling reporters after tabling the Kedah Budget 2027 at Wisma Darul Aman here.
He said the result also carried a message for the parties concerned, as voters had assessed current political developments for themselves.
Asked about his lighter presence on the Melaka campaign trail, Muhammad Sanusi said he had to concentrate on preparing the state budget, which required close scrutiny.
“I need to focus on Kedah Budget 2027 because it is longer, takes more time and is more detailed.
“We have to focus properly on the presentation, so there was no time. But there are plenty of others,” he was quoted as saying.
In yesterday’s Melaka election, BN won 21 of the 28 state seats while the PAS-led PN three, giving the two sides a two-thirds majority between them, while Pakatan Harapan took four.
Bersatu, a PN component party, contested the election under its own logo, separately from PN, after falling out with PAS.

Title: Perikatan to decide stance on Sarawak polls as BN sits out, says Annuar Musa
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) will determine its stance on contesting the upcoming Sarawak state election soon, according to its Information Chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa.
In a Facebook post today, Annuar stated that Barisan Nasional (BN) will not participate in the Sarawak polls, adding that not contesting might also be an option for PN.
This follows an announcement by BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi that the coalition will not contest any seats in the 13th Sarawak state election.
“BN has no intention of contesting any state seats in Sarawak, as this is the understanding between Umno and PBB in the state,” Zahid said.
Zahid, who is also Umno president and Deputy Prime Minister, explained that the decision aligns with the existing understanding between Umno and Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB).
The Election Commission has set December 12 as polling day for the Sarawak election, with nominations scheduled for November 28.

Title: GRS MPs to submit memorandum to PAC, seek expanded Pan Borneo probe
Article:
PAPAR, Nov 15 — Seven Gabungan Rakyat Sabah (GRS) Members of Parliament will submit a memorandum to the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) next week seeking an expanded scope of investigation into the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project, including an examination of the basis and implications of the decision to terminate the Project Delivery Partner (PDP) model in 2019.
Papar MP Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali. their spokesman, said the move was important to ensure that the PAC investigation not only focused on the project’s current status and performance, but also examined previous policy decisions allegedly affecting its implementation schedule, contractor appointments and rising construction costs.
Armizan, who is also GRS secretary-general, welcomed the PAC’s decision on October 19 to investigate the management, financial governance and physical implementation of the project following the tabling of the Auditor-General’s Report (AG’s Report) Series 2/2026.
However, he said the scope of the investigation should cover four key factors relating to the termination of the PDP model on September 22, 2019, to comprehensively identify the actual causes of the project’s delays.
“That is our recommendation to the PAC, that the scope of the investigation be expanded to cover the basis and implications of the termination of the PDP model,” he told reporters after officiating at the closing ceremony of the IP SPARK 2026 programme here today.
Elaborating, Armizan said the first factor was the lack of clarity regarding the implications of the PDP termination in the AG’s Report Series 2/2026, although official responses by the Works Ministry in the Dewan Rakyat on August 2, 2022 and October 19, 2026 had cited the termination of the model as one of the causes of project delays.
“So this is not political talk or political issues determined by people, but an official response in the Dewan Rakyat,” said Armizan, who is also Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister.
The second factor, he said, was the need to obtain clarification on the basis of the Federal Government’s decision to terminate the PDP model in 2019 following a recommendation by the Sabah state administration at the time, including whether a comprehensive study had been conducted before the decision was made.
On the third factor, he said uncertainty over the status of the PDP and contractor appointments following the change of government in May 2018 had allegedly caused construction work on the ground to stall for more than a year before existing contractors were reappointed under the conventional implementation method in 2019.
The disruption was also alleged to have contributed to higher project costs, particularly as contractors faced increases in construction material prices due to inflation, as well as the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic.
He said the fourth factor involved the process of reappointing existing contractors and appointing new ones, which was disrupted following the transition from the PDP model to the conventional method, resulting in some Phase 1A packages only undergoing the appointment process in 2021.
“So we hope that not only government agencies but also the contractors will be called to these proceedings to hear about the pressures and issues they faced,” he said.
He stressed that the GRS memorandum was not intended to find fault with any party, but to ensure that policy decisions concerning public infrastructure projects were not influenced by partisan political considerations to the detriment of their smooth implementation. — Bernama

Title: With MIC’s backing, BN vows to field PPP candidates in upcoming general election, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 15 — Barisan Nasional (BN) is committed to fielding candidates from the People’s Progressive Party (PPP) to represent the coalition in the upcoming 16th General Election (GE16).
BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said PPP president Datuk Dr Loga Bala Mohan remained steadfast alongside other coalition partners in efforts to revitalise the party as a new component member of BN.
“In my heart, alongside our partners from Umno, MCA and MIC, the PPP is also our partner.
“With the agreement of Tan Sri SA Vigneswaran (MIC president) and Datuk Seri M. Saravanan (MIC deputy president), I am determined that we will field PPP candidates in the upcoming general election,” he said in his speech at the Malaysia PPP Deepavali Open House here today.
On January 18, it was reported that PPP had been officially accepted as a component party of BN.
The Registrar of Societies (RoS), in a letter dated November 25, 2025, confirmed PPP’s status as a component party within the coalition. — Bernama

Title: Parit Yaani crash: Johor govt to bear medical costs, provide monthly aid to orphaned siblings, says exco
Article:
BATU PAHAT, Nov 15 — The Johor government, through the Johor State Islamic Religious Council (MAINJ), will cover the medical costs, including plastic surgery, for the two orphaned siblings who survived an accident along Jalan Yong Peng-Muar, near Parit Yaani, on November 1.
State Islamic Religious Affairs Committee chairman Mohd Fared Mohd Khalid said the assistance would also include a monthly allowance, as both children were orphaned following the tragedy.
He said the elder sibling, 11-year-old Hasya Fahira Zulkifli, had been readmitted to hospital and was scheduled to undergo plastic surgery on her leg, while her younger brother, Muhammad Adam Mohd Hardi, 8, was now able to walk but still required several follow-up treatments.
“MAINJ’s monthly financial assistance will continue until both siblings receive Survivors’ Pension benefits from the Social Security Organisation (PERKESO), as we understand their father had made contributions.
“The state government will continue to monitor the progress of both siblings… besides MAINJ, we have also been informed that the Social Welfare Department (JKM) is providing assistance,” he told reporters today.
He said this after accompanying Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi to visit Hasya Fahira at a ward at Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital (HSNI), where they also celebrated her 11th birthday today.
Elaborating, Mohd Fared said the state government was also prepared to cover other expenses should the need arise.
“Assistance of this nature is not limited to these two siblings but is extended to all Johoreans in need,” he added.
In the November 1 accident, which occurred at about 12.30pm, the siblings’ parents, Tengku Syafirana Tengku Abdullah, 44, and Mohd Hardi Mohd Husin, 46, were killed after the multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) they were traveling in was crushed by a tar-laden lorry, which had skidded following a tyre blowout.
In the incident, Mohd Hardi sustained serious injuries to his head and both hands, as well as burns to his body, while Tengku Syafirana suffered serious head and internal injuries, as well as burns to her body. — Bernama

Title: Vehicles over 5m barred from Sibu road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang until Feb 28 for festive decor
Article:
SIBU, Nov 15 — Vehicles exceeding five metres in height are prohibited from entering a designated road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang until Feb 28, 2027 to accommodate Christmas street lighting and festive decorations.
Sibu Municipal Council (SMC) in a statement said the restriction, which took effect on November 14, applies to the road section beside Dataran Tun Tuanku Bujang, behind the WTK Holdings Berhad building.
The council said the temporary measure was necessary to ensure public safety as Christmas decorations and lighting installations would be suspended above the roadway.
SMC advised transport operators, lorry drivers, business operators and members of the public to plan their journeys accordingly and comply with all on-site instructions.
Meanwhile, the council said the Sibu Christmas Celebration 2026, themed ‘Lighting Up Sibu, Celebrating Christmas Together’, aimed to bring the community together, promote cultural harmony and share the joy of the festive season.
“Through the celebration, the council hopes to create a warm, joyful and welcoming festive environment where families, friends, residents and visitors of all ages can gather and enjoy the Christmas spirit,” it said.
SMC added that Christmas symbolised love, peace, hope and the spirit of giving, values that transcended racial, religious and cultural boundaries.
The council said the festive lighting and activities were also expected to enhance Sibu’s appeal, attract visitors and create business opportunities for local traders, food operators and the tourism industry.
SMC thanked the public for their understanding and cooperation in observing the temporary restriction and invited everyone to take part in the Christmas celebration. — The Borneo Post

Title: Senator warns early Parliament dissolution could derail Budget 2027 and force temporary spending, citing 2022 precedent
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 15 — Calls for an early dissolution of the Dewan Rakyat are ill-timed as Budget 2027 has yet to complete the parliamentary approval process, said Senator Datuk Ahmad Ibrahim.
He said dissolving Parliament before the Budget was passed could disrupt the government’s financial planning and delay funding for development projects, infrastructure programmes and other public commitments.
Ahmad said that while the Prime Minister could seek the dissolution of Parliament under the Federal Constitution, subject to the discretion of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the timing of such a move should be carefully considered.
“My concern is not about whether Parliament can be dissolved, but whether this is the appropriate time to do so,” he said in a statement.
Ahmad, who chairs the Senate Select Committee on National Defence and Security, pointed out that Budget 2027, involving hundreds of billions of ringgit in government expenditure, was still undergoing parliamentary scrutiny.
The Dewan Rakyat is scheduled to complete its committee-stage deliberations on November 26, while the Dewan Negara will begin its deliberations on November 30.
Ahmad said the legislative process should be allowed to run its course, warning that dissolving Parliament before the Supply Bill completes the approval process could result in it lapsing.
“This would require a new government and Parliament to reintroduce and approve the Budget, potentially delaying financial authorisations needed to sustain government operations and implement planned programmes.
“Although temporary expenditure arrangements could be made under constitutional provisions, these would still require further legislative action,” he said.
He cited the October 2022 dissolution of Parliament, which took place just three days after Budget 2023 was tabled.
Following the formation of a new government, Parliament had to approve about RM107.7 billion in temporary operating expenditure in December 2022 to ensure that government operations could continue pending approval of the full Budget.
“Why unnecessarily risk repeating such complications?”
Ahmad said Malaysia was already facing an increasingly uncertain global environment, marked by geopolitical tensions, economic instability, employment concerns, food security issues and the rising cost of living.
